texts.name: 1. Build exactly the 5 frames below, named exactly as listed (one state per frame), and wire them as a clickable prototype with the listed links. 2. Everything in “Must include” must appear on that frame. The lists are grouped by subject and sorted alphabetically — they are not in page order and say nothing about layout, grouping, emphasis or styling. Those are your decisions. 3. The two brand colors and the typeface in 01 · Foundations are fixed. Define every other color yourself, plus type scale, spacing, radii, elevation and the page grid, and apply them consistently. 4. 02 · Components gives only a default Button and a default Text Field. Design all other states, the header, the footer, the navigation and every business component as reusable components in your file. 5. Use the wordmark, the social logos, the photos, the category images, the decorations, the avatars and the icons from 04 · Media. 6. Copy and data must match “Fixed data” exactly. This brief wins over anything you may know of the original kit.
texts.text:
1. Build exactly the 5 frames below, named exactly as listed (one state per frame), and wire them as a clickable prototype with the listed links.
2. Everything in “Must include” must appear on that frame. The lists are grouped by subject and sorted alphabetically — they are not in page order and say nothing about layout, grouping, emphasis or styling. Those are your decisions.
3. The two brand colors and the typeface in 01 · Foundations are fixed. Define every other color yourself, plus type scale, spacing, radii, elevation and the page grid, and apply them consistently.
4. 02 · Components gives only a default Button and a default Text Field. Design all other states, the header, the footer, the navigation and every business component as reusable components in your file.
5. Use the wordmark, the social logos, the photos, the category images, the decorations, the avatars and the icons from 04 · Media.
6. Copy and data must match “Fixed data” exactly. This brief wins over anything you may know of the original kit.

texts.name: Intro: A quick weeknight fried rice that turns leftover rice into a light, healthy meal. Crisp asparagus, soft eggs and a simple soy-sesame sauce come together in one pan in about 30 minutes. Nutrition note: Values are per serving and approximate.
texts.text:
Intro: A quick weeknight fried rice that turns leftover rice into a light, healthy meal. Crisp asparagus, soft eggs and a simple soy-sesame sauce come together in one pan in about 30 minutes.
Nutrition note: Values are per serving and approximate.

texts.name: For main dish: 2 cups cooked jasmine rice, chilled overnight (checked) · 1 bunch asparagus, cut into 2 cm pieces · 2 eggs, beaten · 2 spring onions, thinly sliced · 1 tbsp neutral oil For the sauce: 2 tbsp soy sauce · 1 tsp sesame oil · 1 tsp mirin
texts.text:
For main dish: 2 cups cooked jasmine rice, chilled overnight (checked) · 1 bunch asparagus, cut into 2 cm pieces · 2 eggs, beaten · 2 spring onions, thinly sliced · 1 tbsp neutral oil

texts.name: Intro: We asked a working head chef about first jobs, long services and what it really takes to make it in a professional kitchen. How did you start out in the food industry? — I started washing dishes in a small family restaurant when I was sixteen. Watching the line cooks every night made me want to be on the other side of the pass, and after two years the chef finally let me prep vegetables. What do you like most about your job? — The rhythm of service. Hours of preparation come down to a few intense minutes, and when a full dining room goes quiet because everyone is eating, it feels like the whole team has done something together.

Intro: We asked a working head chef about first jobs, long services and what it really takes to make it in a professional kitchen.
How did you start out in the food industry? — I started washing dishes in a small family restaurant when I was sixteen. Watching the line cooks every night made me want to be on the other side of the pass, and after two years the chef finally let me prep vegetables.
What do you like most about your job? — The rhythm of service. Hours of preparation come down to a few intense minutes, and when a full dining room goes quiet because everyone is eating, it feels like the whole team has done something together.

texts.name: Do you cook at home on your days off? — Yes, but simply. I cook the food I grew up with: rice, eggs and whatever vegetables look good at the market. Home cooking is where I remember why I love food. [Photo_Cooking_Step] What would your advice be to young people looking to get their foot in the door? — Start anywhere and be the person who shows up early. Ask questions, taste everything and write down what you learn. Pull quote: “Technique can be taught; curiosity and reliability can’t.” What is the biggest misconception that people have about being a professional chef? — That it is all creativity. Most of the job is consistency: making the same dish perfectly two hundred times a night, keeping the kitchen clean and looking after your team.
